title: Communicational Cohesion Overlap
pattern: A function executes multiple operations that use the same input data, but the operations have completely different semantic responsibilities (e.g., printing data AND mutating/deleting that same data).
why_bad: Grouping these operations hides a critical side-effect. A developer who merely wants to print the report will unexpectedly lose their data, violating the principle of least surprise and causing hard-to-track state bugs.
detection: A single method performs a read-only operation (such as rendering or exporting) and also performs a destructive mutation or reset of that same data structure.
counterexample: Atomic operations where clearing or updating state is a fundamental, verified step of the retrieval process (such as a thread-safe Queue `pop()` method).
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete, Chapter 7, Section "Aim for Strong Cohesion" (Communicational Cohesion)*
